limitations: Kirchhoff (thin-plate) theory: a/t = 100 keeps the Mindlin shear correction ~1e-4 relative, but the model carries no transverse shear deformation at all.

Timoshenko table 35 (CCCC) is quoted to three significant digits, so 0.42 % of the reported CCCC error is reference rounding, not discretisation; the extended N=80 level (alpha = 0.001265) sits on that floor and the CCCC order is therefore graded by self-convergence rather than against the table.

The CCCC centre moment converges from above to 0.02291 q a^2 (0.02322, 0.02298, 0.02292, 0.02291 at N=10,20,40,80), i.e. 0.8 % below the three-significant-digit table value 0.0231; the error against the table is therefore non-monotone (it crosses the table value near N=10) even though the moment itself converges at order 2.
The 11x11 Navier truncation mandated by the campaign is accurate for deflections (~5e-8) but only ~1e-3 for the moments; the moment gates use the 301-harmonic evaluation of the same series.

Hard simple support excludes the corner uplift dof; this is the exact Kirchhoff condition and the same convention as benchmarks/verified/fem_plate, so results are comparable but not identical (that anchor used lumped nodal loads).
